clue.text: Film made by two serving US soldiers

indicators.note: two says a pair of soldiers is meant, so the abbreviation is set down side by side with itself

parts.note: a GI is a serving American soldier, giving the first copy
GI is the term for US soldiers, giving the second copy

explanation.surface: A movie produced by a couple of American servicemen on active duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'two' says there are a pair of GIs; serving and US soldiers each supply one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is the 1958 Lerner and Loewe musical picture set in Paris.

clue.text: So sad somehow imbibing last of Portuguese port

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the scrambled letters take the next piece inside them
somehow says the letters of 'So sad' are arranged in some other way
last of picks the final letter of the word Portuguese

explanation.surface: A melancholy person drinking the dregs of their port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal scrambles SO SAD into ODSSA; imbibing puts E, the final letter of Portuguese, inside it. Portuguese port suggests Porto, but this port is on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major seaport on the Black Sea coast of Ukraine.

clue.text: Spread out uniform

definitions.meaning: lying spread out means stretched out level on the ground
even and unvarying, as a monotone voice or a fixed fee is

explanation.surface: Laying out a set of clothes worn by staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat can mean extended horizontally or, as in a flat fee, the same throughout.

clue.text: Swindle American, pocketing gold ring

indicators.note: pocketing means taking something inside, so the gold goes into the other letters

parts.note: a con is a swindle
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A con artist cheating an American and stealing a gold ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts OR inside CONA, between C and ONA.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a circle of light, such as the halo seen round the sun or moon.

clue.text: Awful record on the radio leads to conversation

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only listened to, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: awful is dire and a record is a log, giving 'dire log'

explanation.surface: A dreadful song played on air sparks a chat among listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'dire log' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a talk or exchange of speech between two or more people.

clue.text: Flower, monster, placed under picture

indicators.note: in a down entry the monster sits beneath the picture, so it comes second

parts.note: a snap is a photograph
a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: An illustrated book entry showing a flower and a beast beneath a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant whose blooms look like a mouth.

clue.text: Current trip brings unexpected bonus

parts.note: wind is a current of air
to trip is to fall, or a fall

explanation.surface: An electrical or sea current tripping someone yields a surprise payout.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is literally fruit blown down, hence any unforeseen piece of good fortune.

clue.text: This may be read either way?

definitions.text: This may be read either way?

parts.words: This may be read either way?
parts.note: a light novel is something read, and its letters run the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about something readable forwards or backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga saga is a genre of novel about comfortable English country life, named after the cooking range; it is a palindrome.

clue.text: Feel one's way round one in musical

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the musical's name

parts.note: Rent is a Broadway musical
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Groping about blindly around someone who's in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient oneself is to find one's bearings, gradually working out where one is.

clue.text: Sleep after lunch, beginning to snore, before tea is prepared

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of the word snore
prepared says the letters of 'tea is' are made up afresh

explanation.surface: A post-lunch nap, starting with a snore, before afternoon tea is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is the customary midday nap of hot countries, taken after the main meal.

clue.text: Wheel in drink for writer

indicators.note: in places the wheel word inside the drink word

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
to wheel is to roll

explanation.surface: Pushing a wheelbarrow into a drinking session for a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian novelist of the Barsetshire Chronicles.

clue.text: Involving espionage, conceal article, knife, behind Bond's back

indicators.note: behind puts the knife after the letter from Bond

parts.note: to cloak is to conceal
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: back takes the rear letter of the word Bond's

parts.note: a dagger is a short stabbing knife

explanation.surface: A spy hides something and a blade behind James Bond's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes secretive intrigue typical of spies and undercover plots.

clue.text: Waterway worker's Alice band, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the person who operates a lock on a canal
an Alice band holds back hair, keeping locks in place

explanation.surface: A canal hand wearing a hairband like Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock-keeper tends canal gates; an Alice band, named after Tenniel's Alice, keeps hair tidy.

clue.text: Bird close to long-handled gardening tool

indicators.note: close here means the end, so this takes the final letter of long-handled

parts.note: a rake is a gardening tool

explanation.surface: A bird standing near a long-handled rake in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long-handled gardening tool' reads as one phrase, but 'long-handled' only gives its final D.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by example: a drake is the male of the duck, a water bird.

clue.text: Critically examine small tin

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Inspecting a little tin closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan verse is to analyse its metre, and to scan generally is to scrutinise closely.

clue.text: Newcomer in religious order, one they ordered to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the scrambled letters surround the quiet letter
ordered says the letters of 'one they' are put into a new sequence

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A novice in a monastic order is told to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' is the anagram signal and 'to keep' the container signal. 'religious order' and 'ordered' look like one idea; only the second scrambles letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a novice or new convert, especially one recently admitted to a monastic community.

clue.text: Not living together may become a factor

parts.note: a factor is a part or component of something

explanation.surface: Separated couples may end up as one element among many.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple living apart are separated and do not share a home.

clue.text: Dance with couple on stage

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, puts the couple above the stage

parts.note: a couple is two
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A pair of performers dancing on a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in duple time with sliding steps.

clue.text: Women dropped out of golf club side

indicators.note: dropped out of means removed from, so the letter for women goes

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club

explanation.surface: Female members quit the golf club's team.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the side or border of something.

clue.text: Have expertise — able to tell a scallion from a shallot?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to be well versed in a subject

definitions.text: able to tell a scallion from a shallot?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, the phrase means being able to tell one kind of onion from another

explanation.surface: Being a specialist, perhaps in distinguishing similar vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to be knowledgeable; scallions and shallots are both onion types.

clue.text: Strange story about English shellfish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the English letter
strange says the letters of story are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: An odd tale about an English seafood dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges STORY into OYSTR, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc, eaten raw or prized for pearls.

clue.text: Take no notice of one rig at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of 'one rig' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Overlooking a single oil platform out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it or pay it no attention.

clue.text: Beads scattered across the chapel

indicators.note: across means spread over, so the scrambled beads lie either side of 'the'
scattered says the letters of beads are strewn about anew

explanation.surface: A rosary broken and its beads strewn across a chapel floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' is the anagram signal and 'across' the container signal; Beads looks like rosary beads in the chapel, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda, after the healing pool in John's gospel, is a common name for Welsh nonconformist chapels.

clue.text: Singer in musical, Tommy

indicators.note: in says the answer is concealed within the words 'musical, Tommy'

explanation.surface: A vocalist appearing in the rock musical Tommy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a voice lower than a soprano.

clue.text: Toy with one considering getting rid of husband

indicators.note: getting rid of means discarding, so the husband letter is removed

parts.note: a thinker is one who considers

explanation.surface: A wife playfully weighing up whether to ditch her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker with something is to fiddle or play about with it idly.

clue.text: Presenting no problems when planted in middle of vineyard

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so the word for when goes into the central letters
middle of takes the central pair of letters of vineyard

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Vines growing trouble-free when put in the centre of a vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means simple or straightforward, causing no difficulty.

clue.text: Annoy the Parisian after final

indicators.note: after puts the French article behind the final word

parts.note: nett, a British spelling of net, means final, as in nett profit after deductions
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman irritated after losing a final.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate or provoke them, like a nettle's sting.

clue.text: Better money for army chiefs, maybe

parts.note: to top is to better or surpass
brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Generals being paid more money, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS for money is everyday northern British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is slang for the most senior officers, from the gold braid on their caps.
